question.worked_solution:
At $x=1,$ the left-sided limit is

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to {1}^{-}}h(x) & ={lim}_{x\to {1}^{-}}{e}^{bx} \\  & ={e}^{b(1)} \\  & ={e}^{b},\end{aligned}
$$

 

and the right-sided limit is

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to {1}^{+}}h(x) & ={lim}_{x\to {1}^{+}}(3{x}^{2}-2) \\  & =3(1)^{2}-2 \\  & =1.\end{aligned}
$$

In order for $h(x)$ to be continuous at $x=1,$ we require that

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to {1}^{-}}h(x) & ={lim}_{x\to {1}^{+}}h(x) \\ {e}^{b} & =1 \\ {e}^{b} & ={e}^{0} \\ b & =0.\end{aligned}
$$
